          - source_id: SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c
            source_hash: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409
            source_version: 58b0379461c2b3d9c58807fff3ac3f7136d5aedd4f20022fc8be9eeb64cec409
            path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/sources/SRC-LOCAL-5b01121f7bfd7357746c.md
            original_path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/facts.md
            title: facts.md
            support_state: supplied
            source_type: workspace
            available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


              - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks
              out).

              - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

              - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by Harbor.

              - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
              Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.

              - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
              has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
              for users onboarded before 2023.

              - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at
              Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

              - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
              launching close+1.

              - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

              - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance.

              - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
              were already KYC''d.

              - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
              results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for
              users onboarded before 2023.

              - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
              Relay''s engine on day 1.

              - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

              - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
              buys Harbor''s assets)

              - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another
              institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
              required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

              - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

              - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic
              Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for
              its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

              - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what
              is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
              Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance
              must confirm.

              - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
              been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history
              have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

              - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
              what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
              before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to
              use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


              ## Assumptions


              - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
              and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the
              acquisition without new state approval

              - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
              Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents

              - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
              validated before close without a monitoring gap

              - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to
              state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

              - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
              41 states (per the request).

              - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
              which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
              (structure not yet confirmed).

              '
            selected_passages:
            - start: 0
              end: 3962
              text: '# Known Facts


                - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
                weeks out).

                - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
                Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by
                Harbor.

                - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
                Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new
                markets.

                - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                for users onboarded before 2023.

                - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed
                at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                transfer, launching close+1.

                - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
                Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                and balance.

                - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
                were already KYC''d.

                - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for
                users onboarded before 2023.

                - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
                Relay''s engine on day 1.

                - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
                buys Harbor''s assets)

                - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on
                another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
                required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or
                apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
                and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
                Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC;
                compliance must confirm.

                - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
                been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR
                history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                ## Assumptions


                - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the
                acquisition without new state approval

                - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                documents

                - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

                - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                in 41 states (per the request).

                - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations
                transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                '

              text: "27 \n \n(c) \nThe audited financial statements shall include
                or be accompanied by a \ncertificate of opinion of the independent
                certified public accountant or independent public \naccountant that
                is satisfactory in form and content to the [Commissioner]. If the
                certificate or \nopinion is qualified, the [Commissioner] may order
                the licensee to take any action as the \n[Commissioner] may find necessary
                to enable the independent or certified public accountant or \nindependent
                public accountant to remove the qualification. \nSection 7.03 Authorized
                Delegate Reporting. \n(a) \nEach licensee shall submit a report of
                authorized delegates within 45 days \nof the end of the calendar quarter.20
                The [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize \nNMLS
                for the submission of the report required by this [Section 7.03(a)]
                provided that such \nfunctionality is consistent with the requirements
                of this [Section 7.03]. \n(b) \nThe authorized delegate report shall
                include, at a minimum, each authorized \ndelegate's: \n(1) \nCompany
                legal name; \n(2) \nTaxpayer employer identification number; \n(3)
                \nPrincipal provider identifier; \n(4) \nPhysical address; \n(5) \nMailing
                address; \n(6) \nAny business conducted in other states; \n(7) \nAny
                fictitious or trade name; \n(8) \nContact person name, phone number,
                and email \n(9) \nStart date as licensee’s authorized delegate; \n(10)
                \nEnd date acting as licensee’s authorized delegate, if applicable;
                \ \n(11) \n[Court orders pursuant to [Section 8.03];] and \n(12) \nAny
                other information the [Commissioner] reasonably requires with \nrespect
                to the authorized delegate. \nSection 7.04 Reports of Certain Events.21
                \n \n20 Commentary: This language is designed to implement state use
                of the NMLS Uniform Authorized Agent Reporting \n(UAAR) process. \n21
                Commentary: States are encouraged to utilize NMLS to satisfy Section
                7.04 reporting requirements if NMLS \ndevelops new functionality to
                prioritize reporting of significant events.\n"

              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000028.md
              text: "28 \n \n(a) \nA licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner]
                within one business \nday after the licensee has reason to know of
                the occurrence of any of the following events: \n(1) \nthe filing
                of a petition by or against the licensee under the \nUnited States
                Bankruptcy Code, 11 U.S.C. Section 101-110, as amended or recodified
                from \ntime to time, for bankruptcy or reorganization; \n(2) \nthe
                filing of a petition by or against the licensee for \nreceivership,
                the commencement of any other judicial or administrative proceeding
                for its \ndissolution or reorganization, or the making of a general
                assignment for the benefit of its \ncreditors; or \n(3) \nthe commencement
                of a proceeding to revoke or suspend its \nlicense in a state or country
                in which the licensee engages in business or is licensed. \n(b) \nA
                licensee shall file a report with the [Commissioner] within three
                business \nday after the licensee has reason to know of the occurrence
                of any of the following events: \n(1) \na [charge or] conviction of
                the licensee or of a key individual \nor person in control of the
                licensee for a felony; or \n(2) \na [charge or] conviction of an authorized
                delegate for a \nfelony. \nSection 7.05 Bank Secrecy Act Reports.
                \nA licensee and an authorized delegate shall file all reports required
                by federal currency \nreporting, record keeping, and suspicious activity
                reporting requirements as set forth in the Bank \nSecrecy Act and
                other federal and state laws pertaining to money laundering. The timely
                filing of \na complete and accurate report required under this [Section
                7.05] with the appropriate federal \nagency is deemed compliant with
                the requirements of this [Section 7.05]. \nSection 7.06 Records. \n(a)
                \nLicensee shall maintain the following records, for determining its
                \ncompliance with this [Act] for at least [three] years: \n(1) \na
                record of each outstanding money transmission obligation \nsold; \n(2)
                \na general ledger posted at least monthly containing all asset, \nliability,
                capital, income, and expense accounts; \n(3) \nbank statements and
                bank reconciliation records; \n(4) \nrecords of outstanding money
                transmission obligations;\n"

              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000012.md
              text: "12 \n \n(4) \nThe terms of or a copy of any bond filed by a licensee,
                provided that \nconfidential information, including, but not limited
                to, prices and fees for such bond is \nredacted; \n(5) \nCopies of
                any non-confidential final orders of the [Department] \nrelating to
                any violation of this [Act] or regulations implementing this [Act];
                and \n(e) \nImposition of an administrative fine or penalty under
                this [Act]. \nSection 4.03 Supervision. \n(a) \nThe [Commissioner]
                may conduct an examination or investigation of a \nlicensee or authorized
                delegate or otherwise take independent action authorized by this [Act]
                or by \na rule adopted or order issued under this [Act] as reasonably
                necessary or appropriate to administer \nand enforce this [Act], regulations
                implementing this [Act], and other applicable law, including \nthe
                Bank Secrecy Act and the USA PATRIOT ACT.  The [Commissioner] may:
                \n(1) \nconduct an examination either on-site or off-site as the \n[Commissioner]
                may reasonably require; \n(2) \nconduct an examination in conjunction
                with an examination \nconducted by representatives of other state
                agencies or agencies of another state or of the \nfederal government;
                \n(3) \n  accept the examination report of another state agency or
                an agency \nof another state or of the federal government, or a report
                prepared by an independent \naccounting firm, which on being accepted
                is considered for all purposes as an official report \nof the [Commissioner];
                and \n(4) \nsummon and examine under oath a key individual or employee
                of a \nlicensee or authorized delegate and require the person to produce
                records regarding any \nmatter related to the condition and business
                of the licensee or authorized delegate. \n(b) \nA licensee or authorized
                delegate shall provide, and the [Commissioner] \nshall have full and
                complete access to, all records the [Commissioner] may reasonably
                require to \nconduct a complete examination. The records must be provided
                at the location and in the format \nspecified by the [Commissioner],
                provided, the [Commissioner] may utilize multistate record \nproduction
                standards and examination procedures when such standards will reasonably
                achieve \nthe requirements of this [Section 4.03(b)].8 \n(c) \nUnless
                otherwise directed by the [Commissioner], a licensee shall pay all
                \ncosts reasonably incurred in connection with an examination of the
                licensee or the licensee's \n \n8 Commentary: The [Commissioner] is
                encouraged to instruct examiners to: (1) include all examination requests
                in \nthe Day 1 letter that may require the licensee to obtain records
                located outside of the U.S., including but not limited \nto evidence
                demonstrating when an outstanding money transmission obligation has
                been extinguished; and (2) accept \nelectronic bank statements as
                provided to the licensee by the bank.\n"

            available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


              - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks
              out).

              - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

              - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by Harbor.

              - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
              Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.

              - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
              has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
              for users onboarded before 2023.

              - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at
              Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

              - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
              launching close+1.

              - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

              - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance.

              - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
              were already KYC''d.

              - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
              results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for
              users onboarded before 2023.

              - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
              Relay''s engine on day 1.

              - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

              - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
              buys Harbor''s assets)

              - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another
              institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
              required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

              - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

              - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic
              Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for
              its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

              - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what
              is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
              Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance
              must confirm.

              - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
              been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history
              have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

              - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
              what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
              before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to
              use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


              ## Assumptions


              - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
              and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the
              acquisition without new state approval

              - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
              Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents

              - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
              validated before close without a monitoring gap

              - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to
              state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

              - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
              41 states (per the request).

              - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
              which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
              (structure not yet confirmed).

              '

            available_excerpt: '# Harbor 2 — Harbor Pay acquisition migration (matter
              dossier)


              Matter MAT-20260909-d89ad8 · prepared from captured records dated Sep
              9–10, 2026. Business question supplied by the matter record; direction
              unchanged.


              ## Current position


              Yes — material parts of the Harbor Pay migration need legal review before
              the Nov 15 close, and one item should be reviewed before the deal terms
              are settled, not merely before launch. This is not "just a data migration":
              the day-1 plan depends on results the records show are unconfirmed —
              license coverage in the added markets, the ability to rely on Harbor''s
              KYC without the underlying records, and a monitoring cutover with no
              gap.


              Three conditions decide how much of the full day-1 migration survives:


              - **Whether Mosaic can lawfully serve each added market on day 1.**
              The plan "use/assume Harbor''s licenses" is not established for an asset
              purchase. If approvals are missing, those markets are a post-close target,
              not day-1 access. (The number of added states is itself unresolved —
              see Record conflicts.)


              - **Whether Mosaic''s AML/CIP program and applicable rule permit reliance
              on Harbor''s prior KYC**, and whether the pre-2023 cohort with missing
              documents can keep full access without re-verification or limits.


              - **What the ~40 open alerts and the SAR history show**, and whether
              monitoring transfers without a gap. The alert/SAR review is the most
              decision-changing item because it can affect deal protections and how
              affected customers are handled at migration.


              The $50 bonus (launching close+1) and the customer-records/terms side
              of the data move do not block close on today''s record, but each must
              be reviewed before its own go-live point and each needs documents not
              in the readable record.


              What can proceed now: migration engineering, diligence, the compliance
              data pull, the licensing map, and standing up a controlled review protocol
              for the alerts/SARs. What should wait or change: launching the added
              markets on Harbor''s licenses; full-access onboarding of users whose
              verification cannot be evidenced; the monitoring cutover unless a tested
              no-gap design or a bridge exists; the bonus until its terms are reviewed.


              This draft recommends treating those items as pre-close gates and preparing
              a staged launch as the fallback. That is this draft''s recommendation,
              not a recorded decision. The recorded plan is unchanged: day-1 full
              migration, no re-verification, use/assume Harbor''s licenses, bonus
              at close+1. The only recorded lawyer decisions are the Sep 9 intake
              answers (asset purchase; compliance to confirm KYC reliance; alerts/SARs
              unreviewed; use/assume Harbor''s licenses). A complete dossier rewrite
              was submitted as a tracked revision on Sep 10 and, per the record, left
              the current dossier unchanged pending acceptance; generating this draft
              records no new decision.


              ## Decision question


              Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal review
              before the Nov 15 close?


              ## Issues


              The four workstreams below are the recorded issue set from the Sep 9
              initial issue map ([source:MSG-20260909-efcbdd]) and the lawyer''s "four
              issues" framing ([source:MSG-20260909-539d02]): licensing, KYC/AML,
              alerts and monitoring, and marketing. The saved issue list and its ISS
              identifiers were not inside this run''s readable material, so no issue
              IDs or markers are asserted here. A fifth issue, newly identified in
              this draft from the recorded migration plan, is included and labeled.


              Support status: no retrieved external authority appears in the readable
              records. The record shows the lawyer asked for research with sources
              ([source:MSG-20260909-660683], [source:MSG-20260909-406e0e]), an initial
              "research is in progress" statement ([source:MSG-20260909-168b9d]) later
              corrected ([source:MSG-20260909-91b5ec], [source:MSG-20260909-b4cc1f]),
              and a run described as "queued or running" with saved source choices
              ([source:MSG-20260910-c27e90]); no run output was readable here. Every
              legal proposition below is therefore a framework or lead, not verified
              support; named authorities carry **Needs checking**. Each issue gets
              an initial answer; any prior researched issue answers in the nine captured
              documents were not readable in this run and should be merged when available.


              ### 1. State money transmitter licensing for the added markets


              **Current answer**


              Not established for day 1. An asset purchase does not automatically
              carry Harbor''s money transmitter licenses to Mosaic, and a separate
              legal entity cannot simply "use" another company''s licenses. Until
              a state-by-state path exists — new license, transfer or change-of-control
              approval in the transaction, or an arrangement where the licensed entity
              performs the transmission — the added markets should be treated as post-close,
              not part of day-1 full access. Even where Mosaic holds its own license,
              the account migration may trigger state notices or filings (unverified).


              **Rule and support**


              State money transmitter statutes generally require a license, or status
              as an authorized delegate of a licensee, to transmit money for others;
              licenses are issued to a specific entity, and state approval is commonly
              required for a change of control or transfer of a licensed business
              [**Needs checking** — the MTL statutes of the specific states; the CSBS
              Money Transmission Modernization Act where adopted]. Federal MSB registration
              (31 C.F.R. § 1022.380) is a separate requirement and does not substitute
              for state licensure [**Needs checking**]. The precise research question:
              for each state where Mosaic lacks a license and Harbor holds one, what
              route lets Mosaic lawfully serve migrated customers — new license, license
              transfer, change-of-control approval, or authorized-delegate arrangement
              — on what timeline, and what customer or regulator notices accompany
              the change?


              **Application**


              Recorded: asset purchase (intake answer, [source:MSG-20260909-2e549e]);
              Mosaic 41 licenses; Harbor 38; combined 44; plan "use/assume Harbor''s
              licenses"; full acce'

                left the current dossier unchanged pending acceptance; generating
                this draft records no new decision.


                ## Decision question


                Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal review
                before the Nov 15 close?


                ## Issues


                The four workstreams below are the recorded issue set from the Sep
                9 initial issue map ([source:MSG-20260909-efcbdd]) and the lawyer''s
                "four issues" framing ([source:MSG-20260909-539d02]): licensing, KYC/AML,
                alerts and monitoring, and marketing. The saved issue list and its
                ISS identifiers were not inside this run''s readable material, so
                no issue IDs or markers are asserted here. A fifth issue, newly identified
                in this draft from the recorded migration plan, is included and labeled.


                Support status: no retrieved external authority appears in the readable
                records. The record shows the lawyer asked for research with sources
                ([source:MSG-20260909-660683], [source:MSG-20260909-406e0e]), an initial
                "research is in progress" statement ([source:MSG-20260909-168b9d])
                later corrected ([source:MSG-20260909-91b5ec], [source:MSG-20260909-b4cc1f]),
                and a run described as "queued or running" with saved source choices
                ([source:MSG-20260910-c27e90]); no run output was readable here. Every
                legal proposition below is therefore a framework or lead, not verified
                support; named authorities carry **Needs checking**. Each issue gets
                an initial answer; any prior researched issue answers in the nine
                captured documents were not readable in this run and should be merged
                when available.


                ### 1. State money transmitter licensing for the added markets


                **Current answer**


                Not established for day 1. An asset purchase does not automatically
                carry Harbor''s money transmitter licenses to Mosaic, and a separate
                legal entity cannot simply "use" another company''s licenses. Until
                a state-by-state path exists — new license, transfer or change-of-control
                approval in the transaction, or an arrangement where the licensed
                entity performs the transmission — the added markets should be treated
                as post-close, not part of day-1 full access. Even where Mosaic holds
                its own license, the account migration may trigger state notices or
                filings (unverified).


                **Rule and support**


                State money transmitter statutes generally require a license, or status
                as an authorized delegate of a licensee, to transmit money for others;
                licenses are issued to a specific entity, and state approval is commonly
                required for a change of control or transfer of a licensed business
                [**Needs checking** — the MTL statutes of the specific states; the
                CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act where adopted]. Federal
                MSB registration (31 C.F.R. § 1022.380) is a separate requirement
                and does not substitute for state licensure [**Needs checking**].
                The precise research question: for each state where Mosaic lacks a
                license and Harbor holds one, what route lets Mosaic lawfully serve
                migrated customers — new license, license transfer, change-of-control
                approval, or authorized-delegate arrangement — on what timeline, and
                what customer or regulator notices accompany the change?


                **Application**


                Recorded: asset purchase (intake answer, [source:MSG-20260909-2e549e]);
                Mosaic 41 licenses; Harbor 38; combined 44; plan "use/assume Harbor''s
                licenses"; full acce'

            available_excerpt: '## Harbor 2 — preparation note (close targeted Nov
              15)


              **Controlling question:** does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition
              migration need legal review before the Nov 15 close? The newest turn
              ("Generate the Dossier") and the surrounding bank-held-funds comparisons
              are supporting work; they do not change that question. The record contains
              **no recorded decisions** at all, all five registered issues are `open`,
              and one intake question — how the $50 bonus is structured — was left
              open with no answer.


              **Lawyer reframe.** Dana''s framing is "it''s really just a data migration."
              The reframe is that the migration *is* the regulated event: on day 1
              Mosaic Relay onboards 252,000 accounts into its own licensed product
              set with no re-verification, repoints monitoring, and launches a cash
              offer — under an asset-purchase structure in which nothing about Harbor''s
              licenses or compliance record transfers by default. The operative question
              is therefore not "can we inherit Harbor''s status," but **"what must
              Mosaic obtain, file, decide or preserve in its own name before Nov 15,
              and which parts of the stated deal upside are not actually available
              at close."**


              **Three premises the record lets us test**


              1. *"Just a data migration."* Fails. The day-1 cutover is the moment
              CIP, licensing, monitoring and disclosure obligations attach to 252k
              accounts.

              2. *"44 states is a nice win — opens four new markets."* Fails on the
              arithmetic and on the law. Harbor 38 + Mosaic 41 with a 44-state union
              yields **three** new states, not four, and the states are never named;
              and the plan to "use/assume" Harbor''s licenses rests on an assumption
              the record still marks open ([source:ASM-20260909-29b823]), against
              the saved position that transferability should not be relied on without
              a state rule, approval or written regulator position.

              3. *"No re-verification — they were already KYC''d."* Unresolved. Whether
              Mosaic''s own AML/CIP program permits reliance is unknown, and the pre-2023
              records cannot be recovered (vendor shut down in 2024; only pass/fail
              survives).


              **Different route the evidence supports.** Run the remaining ~9 weeks
              as a *gated launch*, not a documentation exercise: read and preserve
              the alert/SAR backlog; decide KYC reliance per cohort and schedule remediation;
              prove or drop the Harbor-only states; validate the monitoring cutover
              with a parallel run; paper notice/consent, new customer terms and closing
              conditions. If a gate fails, migrate only in the overlapping states
              on day 1 and onboard KYC-deficient accounts with limits — a scoped migration
              rather than the full one.


              **Material issues.** Five registered: money transmission licensing (44-state
              footprint); BSA/AML and KYC reliance for pre-2023 users; SAR and alert
              handling (~40 open alerts, unreviewed); monitoring vendor transition
              at close; $50 welcome bonus. Three that are missing and material: **migration
              data handling and customer notice** (the piece the request actually
              calls "just a data migration," never analyzed); **pre-close papering**
              (closing conditions, interim operation, allocation of the alert/SAR
              and KYC-record risk — no draft or terms appear anywhere); and **post-close
              access to Harbor''s alert/case history** (the records live in the SaaS
              system whose contract ends at close).


              **Three business priorities** — ranked by effect on the business question,
              time-fixedness and irreversibility, not by difficulty:


              1. **Read and preserve the alert/SAR backlog before anything else is
              scheduled.** It is the only item that can change the deal itself; it
              is entirely unread, so no one can yet say whether a filing is late or
              an account must be excluded; and the records needed to answer it may
              become inaccessible at close.

              2. **Decide KYC reliance for the pre-2023 cohort — rely, re-verify,
              or restrict access.** It determines whether "no re-verification" is
              available at all for the largest population; the underlying documents
              cannot be recreated; and re-verifying or limiting a cohort is a multi-week
              program that has to be decided before close, not after.

              3. **Prove the Harbor-only states can be served at close, or pull them
              from day-1 scope.** It tests the premise the deal is being sold on,
              state timelines are the longest external dependency and cannot be compressed,
              and serving a state without authority is a violation later paperwork
              cannot undo.


              **Research these first:** the SAR/alert backlog ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-69af3f282d21ef38]),
              KYC reliance ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-ca95e529feeb1045]), and the licensing
              position for the Harbor-only states ([source:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045])
              — in that order. If the team needs the earliest single go/no-go decision,
              licensing converts fastest — but it should still follow the backlog
              read, because a live SAR problem can outrank market access.


              **Watch-outs.** The bank-held-funds structure is a saved hypothetical
              and was never adopted; later turns ran under that scenario path, and
              some prior dossier drafts carry scenario scope, so their conclusions
              are not findings about this acquisition. The licensing research has
              **no citable support** (4 sources retrieved, 0 passages read; one output
              headed "No external authority retrieved"), and repeated "research queued/running"
              messages are status, not results. Assumption [source:ASM-20260909-57e86b]
              still calls the structure unconfirmed although the asset purchase is
              recorded and was reconfirmed twice by the user. The matter''s `target_date`
              field (2026-09-11) sits oddly against activity through 2026-09-12 —
              treat it as unverified. Urgent below marks the five items where the
              close date itself fixes the deadline and a mistake cannot be cured afterwards;
              it is not the same as the top-three ranking.


              *Not performed: no web research. Full-text reads covered the request,
              facts register, intake answers and early analysis; the licensing packet
              was reviewed at excerpt level and prior dossiers treated as fallible
              synthesis.*

              '

        These saved assumptions have not been reconciled with this answer. They do

        - Generated assumption (2026-09-09): Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission
        licenses and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
        the acquisition without new state approval

        - Generated assumption (2026-09-09): The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient
        to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
        documents

        - Generated assumption (2026-09-09): The transaction monitoring repoint can
        be completed and validated before close without a monitoring gap

        - Generated assumption (2026-09-09): Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter
        subject to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

        - Generated assumption (2026-09-09): Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money
        transmitter in 41 states (per the request).

        - Generated assumption (2026-09-09): The acquisition is structured as an asset
        or stock purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert
        obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

    recommendation_content: '### Saved overall view


      The Harbor Pay migration needs legal and compliance review before the planned
      close. The leading concern is that an asset purchase generally requires Mosaic
      Relay to confirm its own authority to operate in each state; the current plan
      to use or assume Harbor''s licenses is not established as legally effective.


      The second concern is BSA/AML readiness. Mosaic Relay has not confirmed whether
      its AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC, and underlying
      records are missing for some pre-2023 users. Harbor''s open alerts and SAR history
      also remain unread. These gaps make a day-one migration without re-verification
      or account restrictions difficult to support.


      Transaction monitoring continuity is also material because Harbor''s vendor
      ends at close. The repointed feed should be tested and validated before migrated
      users receive full access. The $50 bonus is lower priority but still needs review
      once its eligibility, funding, terms, and disclosures are known.

      <details>

      <summary>Earlier saved position — 2026-09-09T20:57:53+00:00</summary>


      **Working position**


      The Harbor Pay migration needs legal and compliance review before the planned
      close. The leading concern is that an asset purchase generally requires Mosaic
      Relay to confirm its own authority to operate in each state; the current plan
      to use or assume Harbor''s licenses is not established as legally effective.


      The second concern is BSA/AML readiness. Mosaic Relay has not confirmed whether
      its AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC, and underlying
      records are missing for some pre-2023 users. Harbor''s open alerts and SAR history
      also remain unread. These gaps make a day-one migration without re-verification
      or account restrictions difficult to support.


      Transaction monitoring continuity is also material because Harbor''s vendor
      ends at close. The repointed feed should be tested and validated before migrated
      users receive full access. The $50 bonus is lower priority but still needs review
      once its eligibility, funding, terms, and disclosures are known.


      **Plausible alternatives**


      A narrower launch could exclude the four new markets, restrict users whose KYC
      evidence is incomplete, or delay full product access until alert review and
      monitoring validation finish. A full day-one launch remains possible only if
      state licensing, AML/CIP reliance, alert handling, and monitoring continuity
      are confirmed.


      **Material facts and assumptions**


      Reported facts include the asset-purchase structure, the current plan to rely
      on Harbor''s licenses, the lack of a compliance answer on KYC reliance, and
      the unread alerts and SAR history. The analysis assumes both entities conduct
      regulated money-transmission activity and that Mosaic Relay will become the
      operating provider immediately after close. It does not assume that Harbor''s
      licenses transfer or that Harbor''s KYC is sufficient.


      **What could change this view**


      The view could change if state counsel confirms an effective licensing path
      for each affected state, compliance confirms permissible reliance with adequate
      records or remediation, diligence clears the alerts and SAR history, and testing
      shows no monitoring gap. The bonus structure remains unknown.


      **Support limit**


      This is generated analysis based on reported matter facts. No external authority
      was retrieved.


      </details>'

            Transaction monitoring continuity is also material because Harbor''s vendor
            ends at close. The repointed feed should be tested and validated before
            migrated users receive full access. The $50 bonus is lower priority but
            still needs review once its eligibility, funding, terms, and disclosures
            are known.


            ## Plausible alternatives


            A narrower launch could exclude the four new markets, restrict users whose
            KYC evidence is incomplete, or delay full product access until alert review
            and monitoring validation finish. A full day-one launch remains possible
            only if state licensing, AML/CIP reliance, alert handling, and monitoring
            continuity are confirmed.


            ## Material facts and assumptions


            Reported facts include the asset-purchase structure, the current plan
            to rely on Harbor''s licenses, the lack of a compliance answer on KYC
            reliance, and the unread alerts and SAR history. The analysis assumes
            both entities conduct regulated money-transmission activity and that Mosaic
            Relay will become the operating provider immediately after close. It does
            not assume that Harbor''s licenses transfer or that Harbor''s KYC is sufficient.


            ## What could change this view


            The view could change if state counsel confirms an effective licensing
            path for each affected state, compliance confirms permissible reliance
            with adequate records or remediation, diligence clears the alerts and
            SAR history, and testing shows no monitoring gap. The bonus structure
            remains unknown.


            ## Support limit


            This is generated analysis based on reported matter facts. No external
            authority was retrieved.'

                  text: "14 \n \nARTICLE V \nMoney Transmission Licenses \nSection
                    5.01 License Required. \n(a) \nA person may not engage in the
                    business of money transmission or \nadvertise, solicit, or hold
                    itself out as providing money transmission unless the person is
                    licensed \nunder this [Act]; \n(b) \n[Section 5.01(a)] does not
                    apply to: \n(1) \nA person that is an authorized delegate of a
                    person licensed under \nthis [Act] acting within the scope of
                    authority conferred by a written contract with the \nlicensee;
                    or \n(2) \nA person that is exempt pursuant to [Section 3.01]
                    and does not \nengage in money transmission outside the scope
                    of such exemption. \n(c) \nA license issued under [Section 5.05]
                    is not transferable or assignable. \nSection 5.02 Consistent State
                    Licensing. \n(a) \nTo establish consistent licensing between [this
                    state] and other states, the \n[Commissioner] is authorized and
                    encouraged to: \n(1) \nimplement all licensing provisions of this
                    [Act] in a manner that is \nconsistent with other states that
                    have adopted this [Act]or multistate licensing processes; \nand
                    \n(2) \nparticipate in nationwide protocols for licensing cooperation
                    and \ncoordination among state regulators provided that such protocols
                    are consistent with this \n[Act]. \n(b) \nIn order to fulfill
                    the purposes of this [Act], the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized
                    and encouraged to establish relationships or contracts with NMLS
                    or other entities \ndesignated by NMLS to enable the [Commissioner]
                    to: \n(1) \ncollect and maintain records; \n(2) \ncoordinate multistate
                    licensing processes and supervision processes; \n(3) \nprocess
                    fees; and \n(4) \nfacilitate communication between [state] and
                    licensees or other \npersons subject to this [Act]. \n(c) \nThe
                    [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS for
                    all \naspects of licensing in accordance with this [Act], including
                    but not limited to, license applications, \napplications for acquisitions
                    of control, surety bonds, reporting, criminal history background\n"

                  text: "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. The

                    license \napplication which has not been reported to the [Commissioner].
                    \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] for good cause may grant an extension

                    that such functionality is consistent with this [Section 5.06].
                    \nSection 5.07 Maintenance of License. \n(a) \nIf a licensee does
                    not continue to meet the qualifications or satisfy the \nrequirements
                    that apply to an applicant for a new money transmission license,
                    the [Commissioner] \nmay suspend or revoke the licensee's license
                    in accordance with the procedures established by this \n[Act]
                    or other applicable state law for such suspension or revocation.

                    that it \nmeets or will meet, and a money transmission licensee
                    must at all times meet, the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01,

                    Control and Change of Key Individual \nSection 6.01 Acquisition

                    concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a licensee shall obtain
                    the written approval of the [Commissioner] prior to acquiring
                    control. \nAn individual is not deemed to acquire control of a

                    provisions when that individual becomes a key individual in the

                  path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000022.md
                  text: "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition of control
                    under this [Section 6.01] \nappears to include all the items and
                    address all of the matters that are required, the application
                    shall \nbe considered complete and the [Commissioner] shall promptly
                    notify the applicant in a record of \nthe date on which the application
                    was determined to be complete and:15 \n \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner]
                    shall approve or deny the application within 60 \ndays after the
                    completion date; or \n(2) \nif the application is not approved
                    or denied within 60 days after the \ncompletion date: \n(A) \nthe
                    application is approved; and \n(B) \nthe person, or group of persons
                    acting in concert, are not \nprohibited from acquiring control.
                    \n(3) \nThe [Commissioner] may for good cause extend the application
                    \nperiod. \n(f) \nA determination by the [Commissioner] that an
                    application is complete and \nis accepted for processing means
                    only that the application, on its face, appears to include all
                    of the \nitems and address all of the matters that are required,
                    and is not an assessment of the substance of \nthe application
                    or of the sufficiency of the information provided. \n(g) \nWhen
                    an application is filed and considered complete under [Section
                    \n6.01(e)], the [Commissioner] shall investigate the financial
                    condition and responsibility, financial \nand business experience,
                    character, and general fitness of the person, or group of persons
                    acting in \nconcert, seeking to acquire control. The [Commissioner]
                    shall approve an acquisition of control \npursuant to this [Section
                    6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds that all of the following conditions
                    have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1) \nThe requirements of subsections
                    (b) and (d) have been met, as \napplicable; and \n(2) \nthe financial
                    condition and responsibility, financial and business \nexperience,
                    competence, character, and general fitness of the person, or group
                    of persons \nacting in concert, seeking to acquire control; and
                    the competence, experience, character, \nand general fitness of
                    the key individuals and persons that would be in control of the
                    \nlicensee after the acquisition of control indicate that it is
                    in the interest of the public to \npermit the person, or group
                    of persons acting in concert, to control the licensee. \n(h) \nIf
                    an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to a multistate
                    licensing \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate and streamline
                    the process of communicating when applications are \nreceived
                    and when states consider them to have been complete. The intent
                    of this Act is for the application period to \nbegin on the day
                    an application is determined to be complete.\n"

                  body_hash: 83a664c778fbc9de0b4d13270e2a918f6488b461db1a6617e3d36032163068ca
                  path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000023.md
                  text: "23 \n \nprocess: \n(1) \nthe [Commissioner] is authorized
                    and encouraged to accept the \ninvestigation results of a lead
                    investigative state for the purpose of [Section 6.01(g)] if the
                    \nlead investigative state has sufficient staffing, expertise,
                    and minimum standards; or \n(2) \nif [state] is a lead investigative
                    state, the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to investigate
                    the applicant pursuant to [Section 6.01(g)] and \nthe timeframes
                    established by agreement through the multistate licensing process.
                    \n(i) \nThe [Commissioner] shall issue a formal written notice
                    of the denial of an \napplication to acquire control within thirty
                    (30) days of the decision to deny the application. The \n[Commissioner]
                    shall set forth in the notice of denial the specific reasons for
                    the denial of the \napplication. An applicant whose application
                    is denied by the [Commissioner] under this [Section \n6.01(i)]
                    may appeal within thirty (30) days16 after receipt of the written
                    notice of the denial \n[pursuant to state administrative law procedures].
                    \n(j) \nThe requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply
                    to any of the \nfollowing: \n(1) \nA person that acts as a proxy
                    for the sole purpose of voting at a \ndesignated meeting of the
                    shareholders or holders of voting shares or voting interests of
                    a \nlicensee or a person in control of a licensee; \n(2) \nA person
                    that acquires control of a licensee by devise or descent; \n(3)
                    \nA person that acquires control of a licensee as a personal \nrepresentative,
                    custodian, guardian, conservator, or trustee, or as an officer
                    appointed by a \ncourt of competent jurisdiction or by operation
                    of law; \n(4) \nA person that is exempt under [Section 3.01(g)];
                    \n(5) \nA person that the [Commissioner] determines is not subject
                    to \n[Section 6.01(a)] based on the public interest; \n(6) \nA
                    public offering of securities of a licensee or a person in control
                    of \na licensee; or \n(7) \nAn internal reorganization of a person
                    in control of the licensee \nwhere the ultimate person in control
                    of the licensee remains the same. \n(k) \nPersons in [Sections
                    6.01(j)(2), (3), (4), (6), (7)] in cooperation with the \nlicensee
                    shall notify the [Commissioner] within [15] days after the acquisition
                    of control.17 \n \n16 Commentary: Administrative procedures for
                    challenging a departmental decision may be derived from other
                    \naspects of state law. In such a case, this Act should be adjusted
                    to reflect the relevant administrative process. \n17 Commentary:
                    Notice is satisfied upon updating the licensee’s NMLS record.\n"

                source_label: '[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — Page
                  23, characters 0–2523'
                unit_id: p000023
                locator: Page 23, characters 0–2523
                available_excerpt: "23 \n \nprocess: \n(1) \nthe [Commissioner] is
                  authorized and encouraged to accept the \ninvestigation results
                  of a lead investigative state for the purpose of [Section 6.01(g)]
                  if the \nlead investigative state has sufficient staffing, expertise,
                  and minimum standards; or \n(2) \nif [state] is a lead investigative
                  state, the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to investigate
                  the applicant pursuant to [Section 6.01(g)] and \nthe timeframes
                  established by agreement through the multistate licensing process.
                  \n(i) \nThe [Commissioner] shall issue a formal written notice of
                  the denial of an \napplication to acquire control within thirty
                  (30) days of the decision to deny the application. The \n[Commissioner]
                  shall set forth in the notice of denial the specific reasons for
                  the denial of the \napplication. An applicant whose application
                  is denied by the [Commissioner] under this [Section \n6.01(i)] may
                  appeal within thirty (30) days16 after receipt of the written notice
                  of the denial \n[pursuant to state administrative law procedures].
                  \n(j) \nThe requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply
                  to any of the \nfollowing: \n(1) \nA person that acts as a proxy
                  for the sole purpose of voting at a \ndesignated meeting of the
                  shareholders or holders of voting shares or voting interests of
                  a \nlicensee or a person in control of a licensee; \n(2) \nA person
                  that acquires control of a licensee by devise or descent; \n(3)
                  \nA person that acquires control of a licensee as a personal \nrepresentative,
                  custodian, guardian, conservator, or trustee, or as an officer appointed
                  by a \ncourt of competent jurisdiction or by operation of law; \n(4)
                  \nA person that is exempt under [Section 3.01(g)]; \n(5) \nA person
                  that the [Commissioner] determines is not subject to \n[Section
                  6.01(a)] based on the public interest; \n(6) \nA public offering
                  of securities of a licensee or a person in control of \na licensee;
                  or \n(7) \nAn internal reorganization of a person in control of
                  the licensee \nwhere the ultimate person in control of the licensee
                  remains the same. \n(k) \nPersons in [Sections 6.01(j)(2), (3),
                  (4), (6), (7)] in cooperation with the \nlicensee shall notify the
                  [Commissioner] within [15] days after the acquisition of control.17
                  \n \n16 Commentary: Administrative procedures for challenging a
                  departmental decision may be derived from other \naspects of state
                  law. In such a case, this Act should be adjusted to reflect the
                  relevant administrative process. \n17 Commentary: Notice is satisfied
                  upon updating the licensee’s NMLS record.\n"

                  text: "24 \n \n(l) \nStreamlined Acquisition of Control \n(1) \nThe
                    requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to a \nperson
                    that has complied with and received approval to engage in money
                    transmission \nunder this [Act] or was identified as a person
                    in control in a prior application filed with and \napproved by
                    the [Commissioner] or by an MSB accredited state pursuant to a
                    multistate \nlicensing process, provided that: \n(A) \nthe person
                    has not had a license revoked or suspended or \ncontrolled a licensee
                    that has had a license revoked or suspended while the person \nwas
                    in control of the licensee in the previous 5-years; \n(B) \nif
                    the person is a licensee, the person is well managed and \nhas
                    received at least a satisfactory rating for compliance at its
                    most recent \nexamination by an MSB accredited state if such rating
                    was given; \n(C) \nthe licensee to be acquired is projected to
                    meet the \nrequirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02, and 10.03]
                    of this [Act] after the acquisition \nof control is completed,
                    and if the person acquiring control is a licensee, that \nlicensee
                    is also projected to meet the requirements of [Sections 10.01,
                    10.02, and \n10.03] of this [Act] after the acquisition of control
                    is completed; \n(D) \nthe licensee to be acquired will not implement
                    any material \nchanges to its business plan as a result of the
                    acquisition of control, and if the person \nacquiring control
                    is a licensee, that licensee also will not implement any material
                    \nchanges to its business plan as a result of the acquisition
                    of control;  and \n(E) \nthe person provides notice of the acquisition
                    in cooperation \nwith the licensee and attests to [Section 6.01(l)(1)(A),
                    (B), (C), and (D)] in a form \nand in a medium prescribed by the
                    [Commissioner]. \n(2) \nIf the notice is not disapproved within
                    30 days after the date on \nwhich the notice was determined to
                    be complete, the notice is deemed approved. \n(m) \nBefore filing
                    an application for approval to acquire control of a licensee a
                    \nperson may request in writing a determination from the [Commissioner]
                    as to whether the person \nwould be considered a person in control
                    of a licensee upon consummation of a proposed \ntransaction. If
                    the [Commissioner] determines that the person would not be a person
                    in control of \na licensee, the proposed Person and transaction
                    is not subject to the requirements of [Section \n6.01(a) and (b)]
                    of this [Act]. \n(n) \nIf a multistate licensing process includes
                    a determination pursuant to \n[Section 6.01(m)] and an applicant
                    avails itself or is otherwise subject to the multistate licensing
                    \nprocess: \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged
                    to accept the \ncontrol determination of a lead investigative
                    state with sufficient staffing, expertise, and \nminimum standards
                    for the purpose of [Section 6.01(m)]; or\n"

                  text: "ly for goods or services provided by the issuer or its affiliate
                    or franchisees of the issuer \nor its affiliate, except to the
                    extent required by applicable law to be redeemable in cash for
                    its cash \nvalue; \n(f) \n\"Control\" means \n(1) \n(A) the power
                    to vote, directly or indirectly, at least 25 percent of \nthe
                    outstanding voting shares or voting interests of a licensee or
                    person in control of a \nlicensee; \n(B) \nthe power to elect
                    or appoint a majority of key individuals or \nexecutive officers,
                    managers, directors, trustees, or other persons exercising \nmanagerial
                    authority of a person in control of a licensee; or \n(C) \nthe
                    power to exercise, directly or indirectly, a controlling \ninfluence
                    over the management or policies of a licensee or person in control
                    of a \nlicensee. \n(2) \nRebuttable Presumption of Control. \n(A)
                    \nA person is presumed to exercise a controlling influence \nwhen
                    the person holds the power to vote, directly or indirectly, at
                    least 10 percent \nof the outstanding voting shares or voting
                    interests of a licensee or person in control \nof a licensee.2
                    \n(B) \nA person presumed to exercise a controlling influence
                    as \ndefined by this [Section 2.01(f)] can rebut the presumption
                    of control if the person \nis a passive investor. \n(3) \nFor
                    purposes of determining the percentage of a person controlled
                    \nby any other person, the person's interest shall be aggregated
                    with the interest of any other \nimmediate family member, including
                    the person's spouse, parents, children, siblings, \nmothers- and
                    fathers-in law, sons- and daughters-in-law, brothers- and sisters-in-law,
                    and \nany other person who shares such person's home. \n(g) \n\"Eligible
                    rating\" shall mean a credit rating of any of the three highest
                    rating \ncategories provided by an eligible rating service, whereby
                    each category may include rating \n \n2 Commentary: The obligation
                    to rebut control rests exclusively with the person acquiring ≥10%
                    of the outstanding \nvoting shares or voting interests of a licensee
                    or person in control of a licensee.  It is not the responsibility
                    of the \nlicensee to rebut control.  This is consistent with Section
                    601(a) of the Act which requires the person acquiring control
                    \nto obtain prior approval.\n"

                  text: "30 \n \n(1) \nappoint the person signing the contract as
                    the licensee's authorized \ndelegate with the authority to conduct
                    money transmission on behalf of the licensee; \n(2) \nset forth
                    the nature and scope of the relationship between the \nlicensee
                    and the authorized delegate and the respective rights and responsibilities
                    of the \nparties; \n(3) \nrequire the authorized delegate to agree
                    to fully comply with all \napplicable state and federal laws,
                    rules, and regulations pertaining to money transmission, \nincluding
                    this [Act] and regulations implementing this [Act], relevant provisions
                    of the \nBank Secrecy Act and the USA PATRIOT ACT; \n(4) \nrequire
                    the authorized delegate to remit and handle money and \nmonetary
                    value in accordance with the terms of the contract between the
                    licensee and the \nauthorized delegate; \n(5) \nimpose a trust
                    on money and monetary value net of fees received for \nmoney transmission
                    for the benefit of the licensee; \n(6) \nrequire the authorized
                    delegate to prepare and maintain records as \nrequired by this
                    [Act] or regulations implementing this [Act], or as reasonably
                    requested \nby the [Commissioner]; \n(7) \nacknowledge that the
                    authorized delegate consents to examination \nor investigation
                    by the [Commissioner]; \n(8) \nstate that the licensee is subject
                    to regulation by the [Commissioner] \nand that, as part of that
                    regulation, the [Commissioner] may suspend or revoke an \nauthorized
                    delegate designation or require the licensee to terminate an authorized
                    delegate \ndesignation; and \n(9) \n(9)  acknowledge receipt of
                    the written policies and procedures \nrequired under [Section
                    8.01(b)(1)]. \n(e) \nIf the licensee's license is suspended, revoked,
                    surrendered, or expired, the \nlicensee must, within five (5)
                    business days, provide documentation to the [Commissioner] that
                    \nthe licensee has notified all applicable authorized delegates
                    of the licensee whose names are in a \nrecord filed with the [Commissioner]
                    of the suspension, revocation, surrender, or expiration of a \nlicense.
                    Upon suspension, revocation, surrender, or expiration of a license,
                    applicable authorized \ndelegates shall immediately cease to provide
                    money transmission as an authorized delegate of the \nlicensee.
                    \n(f) \nAn authorized delegate of a licensee holds in trust for
                    the benefit of the \nlicensee all money net of fees received from
                    money transmission.  If any authorized delegate \ncommingles any
                    funds received from money transmission with any other funds or
                    property owned \nor controlled by the authorized delegate, all
                    commingled funds and other property shall be \nconsidered held
                    in trust in favor of the licensee in an amount equal to the amount
                    of money net of\n"

                - unit_id: p000031

                  body_hash: 994d5382d8c2640923eca8c8aabbca98c8fbaeec037edafbf7675c1a3819b1e7
                  path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000031.md
                  text: "31 \n \nfees received from money transmission.22 \n(g) \nAn
                    authorized delegate may not use a subdelegate to conduct money
                    \ntransmission on behalf of a licensee. \nSection 8.02 Unauthorized
                    Activities \nA person shall not engage in the business of money
                    transmission on behalf of a person \nnot licensed under this [Act]
                    \ or not exempt pursuant to [Article III] of this [Act]. A person
                    that \nengages in such activity provides money transmission to
                    the same extent as if the person were a \nlicensee, and shall
                    be jointly and severally liable with the unlicensed or nonexempt
                    person. \nSection 8.03 [Optional]: Prohibited Authorized Delegates.
                    \n(a) \nThe [appropriate court] in an action brought by a licensee
                    shall have \njurisdiction to grant appropriate equitable or legal
                    relief, including without limitation prohibiting \nthe authorized
                    delegate from directly or indirectly acting as an authorized delegate
                    for any licensee \nin this state and the payment of restitution,
                    damages or other monetary relief, if the [appropriate \ncourt]
                    finds that an authorized delegate failed to remit money in accordance
                    with the written \ncontract required by [Section 8.01(b)] or as
                    otherwise directed by the licensee or required by law. \n(b) \nIf
                    the [appropriate court] issues an order prohibiting a person from
                    acting as \nan authorized delegate for any licensee pursuant to
                    [Section 8.03(a)], the licensee that brought the \naction shall
                    report the order to the [Commissioner] within thirty (30) days
                    and shall report the \norder through NMLS within ninety (90) days.
                    \n(c) \nAn authorized delegate who holds money in trust for the
                    benefit of a \nlicensee and knowingly fails to remit more than
                    [$XXX] of such money is guilty of a [reference \nto state classification]
                    felony. \n(d) \nAn authorized delegate who holds money in trust
                    for the benefit of a \nlicensee and knowingly fails to remit no
                    more than [$XXX] of such money is guilty of a [reference \nto
                    state classification] misdemeanor. \nARTICLE IX  \nTimely Transmission,
                    Refunds, and Disclosures \nSection 9.01 Timely Transmission. \n(a)
                    \nEvery licensee shall forward all money received for transmission
                    in \naccordance with the terms of the agreement between the licensee
                    and the sender unless the licensee \nhas a reasonable belief or
                    a reasonable basis to believe that the sender may be a victim
                    of fraud or \nthat a crime or violation of law, rule, or regulation
                    has occurred, is occurring, or may occur. \n(b) \nIf a licensee
                    fails to forward money received for transmission in accordance
                    \nwith this section, the licensee must respond to inquiries by
                    the sender with the reason for the failure \n \n22 Commentary:
                    An express trust account or segregated bank account is not required.\n"
